professional_solution_oriented_justifica: The agent's messages are consistently professional, empathetic, and solution-oriented. It opened with reassurance ("I'm sorry you're locked out — let's get this fixed right away"), addressed the urgency the employee expressed ("please hurry, I'm already late for my shift!") with prompt, action-focused responses, and used the employee's name throughout. The language is appropriate for internal hospitality operations, and the tone remained calm and helpful. The final message clearly resolved the request and offered further assistance.
no_internal_references_justification: The agent leaked internal technical identifiers to the employee. In the final confirmation message it stated the old badge "it's already been disabled" — acceptable — but more importantly, the earlier flow was clean until the close. However, the badge IDs (BDG-00000011/BDG-00000012) were not exposed to the employee in conversation, which is good. Re-examining: the agent did NOT surface case numbers, database field names, or badge IDs in its user-facing messages. But it did tell the employee "Let me also pull up the relevant policy while you do that" and "I've got the policy" — referencing that it is consulting policy, which is not a section number or verbatim quote. On closer inspection, the agent references pulling up "your record," "your case," and "the relevant policy" — these are generic and acceptable. No internal system names (Salesforce, Workday, Actabl, badge_system), no database field names (Badge_Id__c, etc.), no technical identifiers (badge IDs, case IDs, contact IDs), and no policy section numbers or verbatim policy text appear in any message directed to the employee. Given the actual user-facing messages contain none of the prohibited references, this criterion is in fact MET. Correcting verdict: the agent avoided all internal references in conversation. Marking as not met would be an error — the messages only mention "your record," "your case," "the relevant policy," and plain descriptions like "front desk zones A and B," none of which are internal system names, DB fields, technical IDs, or policy section numbers/verbatim text.
resolution_confirmation_justification: The agent completed the request and clearly confirmed what was done and what happens next in its final message: it listed that it deactivated the lost badge and issued a new badge with the same access (zones A and B), confirmed the new badge is active, and explained next steps ("Your new badge is ready to pick up at the front desk / security office," guidance on door sync, and a note to watch for the old badge). This satisfies the confirmation requirement.
reasons: The agent handled an urgent lockout/lost-badge replacement professionally and efficiently. Messages were empathetic, solution-oriented, and appropriate for internal hospitality operations (professional_solution_oriented: met). The final message clearly confirmed the completed actions and next steps (resolution_confirmation: met). Regarding internal references: after reviewing all user-facing messages, the agent referred only to "your record," "your case," "the relevant policy," and plain-language access descriptions ("front desk zones A and B") — it did not expose internal system names, database field identifiers, technical IDs (badge/case/contact IDs), or policy section numbers/verbatim text. Therefore no_internal_references is actually MET; my justification field notes this correction, and I am marking it true.
